mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their previous 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS and HOUST fall for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) above its previous 12-month average, without a corresponding rise in employment, signals underemployment expansion, which depresses wage growth and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable, PAYEMS above 12-month average for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is stable but PAYEMS is above its 12-month average for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising above its 5-year average while consumption (GDPC1) grows below its trend) signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and corporate sales, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5-year average and GDPC1 < trend for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS exceeds its 5-year average and GDPC1 grows below trend for six months.
